AuditConfigModel.description:
Deployment audit trail settings. Everything is optional: `event_overrides` switches event types on or off and `sinks` sends events to a git repository or an Integration.

Rules:
- `event_overrides` keys must be known event types.
- Sink names must be unique.
- A sink may not filter on an event type that `event_overrides` has switched off.

event_overrides.description: Switch event types on or off. Keys must be known event types: `deployment.completed`, `deployment.destroyed` and `deployment.measured`, all on by default. Example: `{deployment.measured: false}`.

sinks.description:
Configured audit event destinations

Rules:
- Exactly one of `integration` or `git` must be set, never both and never neither.
- `events` may only list known event types (`deployment.completed`, `deployment.destroyed`, `deployment.measured`).

AuditGitSinkTargetModel.description: Where a git sink pushes: a `remote` declared in the solution manifest (which owns the URL and credentials), the `branch` to push to and a `path` prefix inside the repository.

remote.description: Name of a remote declared in the solution manifest's spec.remotes (strata.yaml). Owns the URL and credentials (via its own `integration`); this sink never declares transport directly.

branch.description: Mutable branch this sink pushes to — distinct from the remote's own (read-pinned) `reference`, refreshed (fetch + reset) immediately before every push.

path.description: Folder inside the repository under which each run's audit files are written.

AuditSinkModel.description:
One destination for audit events. Set exactly one target: `integration` (an Integration document) or `git` (a push to a git remote). `events` limits which event types the sink receives.

Rules:
- Exactly one of `integration` or `git` must be set, never both and never neither.
- `events` may only list known event types (`deployment.completed`, `deployment.destroyed`, `deployment.measured`).

required.description: False (default): a delivery failure only warns. True: a delivery failure fails the run (exit code 3).

events.description: Event filter — None means every gate-admitted event type

integration.description: Name of an Integration document that provides the `audit` capability, such as a `webhook`, `otel` or `sentinel` integration. Each admitted event is sent through it. A delivery failure only warns unless `required` is set.

git.description: Push events to a git repository instead; see `remote`, `branch` and `path`.

name.description: Unique name for the configuration resource.

ConfigurationSecurityModel.description: Allow-lists of the store types that environment documents may use platform-wide for variables, secrets and features, and the key/value backends a workspace may use for step outputs. Each list is closed: anything not listed is rejected, and built-in types such as `constant` or `environment` must be listed to be allowed. Omit a list for no restriction.

allowed_secret_stores.description: Secret store types (SecretStoreType values, e.g. 'azure-keyvault') permitted in any `kind: environment` document. None means unrestricted.

allowed_variable_stores.description: Variable store types (VariableStoreType values, e.g. 'azure-appconfig') permitted in any `kind: environment` document. None means unrestricted.

allowed_feature_stores.description: Feature store types (FeatureStoreType values, e.g. 'azure-appconfig') permitted in any `kind: environment` document. None means unrestricted.

allowed_key_value_stores.description: Key/value backend types (for example `azure-keyvault`, `azure-appconfig`, `azure-blob`) allowed for a workspace's `output_store` and `output_store_integration`. Omit for no restriction.

ConfigurationSpecModel.description:
Platform-wide policy: the provider and topology types in use (by document name), the allowed store types, path naming conventions, audit trail settings and the CVE allow-list. There are no `properties`, `configuration` or `custom` blocks here; values shared across deployments belong in an Environment.

Rules:
- Names in `providers` must be unique.
- Names in `topologies` must be unique.
- Path convention names in `paths` must be unique.

providers.description: Provider type registry: names of ProviderConfig documents

additional_topologies.description: Allow topology types not listed in spec.topologies

topologies.description: Topology type registry: names of TopologyConfig documents

security.description: Allow-lists restricting which store types a variable/secret/feature may declare.

paths.description:
Directory-family naming conventions, checked structurally against real file paths.

Rules:
- `resolves: layers` requires `segments`, because the layers cannot be resolved without them.

audit.description:
Deployment audit trail: local manifest/metrics + optional git/SIEM distribution.

Rules:
- `event_overrides` keys must be known event types.
- Sink names must be unique.
- A sink may not filter on an event type that `event_overrides` has switched off.

cve_allowed.description: Solution-wide list of accepted CVEs, honoured by every workspace's `cve_policy`. Each entry names a CVE id and the reason it is accepted, optionally limited to one package and given an expiry date.

CveAllowedEntryModel.description: One accepted CVE. `id` and `reason` are required; add `package` to limit it to one package and `expires` (an ISO date) to stop honouring it after that day.

package.description: Scope to a specific package name (optional)

expires.description: ISO date after which this entry is ignored (e.g. '2026-12-31')

PathConventionModel.description:
A naming convention for where documents live: for documents under `scope`, the directory must match `pattern` and, optionally, the file name must match `filename_pattern`, both templates with `{segment}` captures. A deployment adopts a convention with `layers.follows`.

Rules:
- `resolves: layers` requires `segments`, because the layers cannot be resolved without them.

name.description: Convention name; a deployment selects it with `layers.follows`.

scope.description: Directory prefix this convention governs, e.g. 'deploy/hubs/**'. Deliberately narrower than a full glob engine — always '<relative-dir>/**'.

pattern.description: Directory template with {segment} captures, e.g. 'deploy/hubs/{hub}/{spoke}/{customer}/{ring}/{environment}'. Matched against a document's containing directory only, relative to the solution root — the filename itself is a separate, independent match (see filename_pattern).

filename_pattern.description: Optional {segment}-capable template matched against just the filename (not the whole path), e.g. 'tenant.yaml' or '{region}.yaml'. None (default) accepts any filename under a directory that matches 'pattern' — not every real convention cares what the file is called.

resolves.description: `tenant`: the single `{code}` capture (from `pattern` or `filename_pattern`) is checked against the name of the Tenant document filed there. `layers`: the convention's `segments` define the layers a deployment is resolved from, so `segments` is required. Omit for a structural shape check only.

segments.description: Per-segment name + validation pattern. Required when resolves == 'layers'.

enforcement.description: `warn` (default) reports a mismatch without failing validation; `deny` fails it.

PathSegmentModel.description: One named capture of a path convention that resolves `layers`: `name` matches a `{name}` placeholder in the convention's `pattern` or `filename_pattern`, and `pattern` is the regex the captured value must match.

name.description: Segment name, matching a {name} capture in pattern or filename_pattern

pattern.description: Regex the captured value must match, e.g. '^[a-z]{3}$' for a 3-letter ring

description: Platform-wide policy for a solution: which provider and topology types exist, which store types are allowed, path naming conventions, audit trail settings and the CVE allow-list. Usually one document, placed where the solution manifest's `spec.configuration` points; several documents there are merged.

apiVersion.description: API version of the configuration model.

meta.description: Name, annotations, labels and tags of this configuration document.

spec.description:
Specification for the configuration.

Rules:
- Names in `providers` must be unique.
- Names in `topologies` must be unique.
- Path convention names in `paths` must be unique.
